title: Sonny: From Ben Dover to Bent Over Backwards, the Commish Who Went Worst to First
body: Every league needs a founding father, and the Buckaroo Football League got Sonny: commissioner, architect of the very website you're reading this on, and for two straight years, the guy holding up the rest of the standings. His debut in 2023 with Ben Dover went 6-8 with 1,413.3 points, good for the 5 seed and, after the consolation ladder had its say, a 6th-place finish out of 6. He made zero trades and 10 pickups, the managerial equivalent of building a house and forgetting to put in doors.

2024 was somehow worse. Ben Dover sank to 5-9, scored 1,304.3 points, grabbed the 6 seed, and finished dead last for the second year running. The defining stat is not the record, though: Sonny made exactly one waiver pickup all season, which is either a bold statement of faith in his roster or proof that the commish was too busy running the league to run his team. The low point came in week 12, when Ben Dover posted 44.1 points against Mekhi, a number that still haunts the archives.

Then came 2025, and the most absurd glow-up in league history. Same team name, completely different energy: Sonny worked the waiver wire 22 times, finally pulled the trigger on a trade, and rode Ben Dover to a 13-3 record, the 1 seed, and a monster 1,850.8 points. His career-best 153.4 came in week 10 against Randy, a beatdown that went down about as well as you'd expect. A perfect 1-0 playoff run later, Sonny hoisted the trophy at Buckaroo Bowl III, ending Kaushal's two-year reign. Did the commissioner rig it? There is no evidence of that whatsoever, which is exactly what a commissioner who rigged it would want you to think.

The head-to-head ledger tells the story of a man who has made enemies on both ends. He owns winning records over Ramon (7-5), Mekhi (7-5), Alan (6-5), and Randy (4-3), but Habib still has his number at 6-5, a fitting reminder of who ran this league before the Ben Dover renaissance. Against the newcomers it's a split: 1-0 over JMoney, 0-1 against Zilgit, who apparently showed up in her first season and decided the defending champ was fair game.

Now rebranded as The Horse is Hea, Sonny sits at 4-2 with 706.9 points and a 10% shot at the title. The habits have stuck: 17 pickups and 2 trades already, meaning the guy who once made one move in a full season has turned into a full-time tinkerer. Maybe it's the Boston air making him soft on loyalty, or maybe he just learned that the waiver wire is where championships are built. Either way, the worst-to-first arc is complete, and the only question left is whether the commish can go back-to-back.
